title: Amazon is being overwhelmed by AI-generated books, and the living space for human authors is being severely squeezed

content_html:
A new study of over 14,000 self-published e-books on Amazon shows that AI-generated content is quietly reshaping the entire publishing market by leveraging its sheer volume. Data indicates that the size of Amazon's book catalog increased by 38.3 times from the beginning of 2023 to the first quarter of 2026, while the platform's quarterly total revenue only grew by 8.9 times during the same period. This means that more and more books are competing for a slowly growing, limited revenue pool, leading to a noticeable "dilution effect" in the market.

What is concerning is that this impact is not limited to low-quality content; even ordinary books without any detectable AI text have also been affected. In the eight major book genres covered in the statistics, the income per book for non-AI texts declined in seven categories. The study points out that books with a large amount of AI content account for 20% of the catalog but contribute only 12.1% and 11.3% to sales and revenue, respectively. Conversely, books without detectable AI text still account for 72.5% of mainstream revenue. However, as AI books continue to climb to the top of bestseller lists, the proportion of AI works in the new Top 25 list has reached as high as 31%.

Additionally, the analysis found that some prolific authors have significantly increased their output using AI, with some authors earning millions of dollars from just a few books. In terms of language features, best-selling AI books show a high degree of overlap with existing published works, relying much more on rare expressions than typical literary works.

Industry experts believe that this study provides key empirical data for ongoing AI copyright lawsuits. In the past, AI companies often defended themselves by citing human reading and learning as justification. However, evidence of market dilution and linguistic overlap may have a profound impact on future judicial judgments regarding fair use.

content_html_zh:
对亚马逊上 14,000 多本自行出版的电子书进行的一项新研究表明，人工智能生成的内容正在利用其庞大的数量悄然重塑整个出版市场。 数据显示，从2023年初到2026年第一季度，亚马逊图书目录规模增长了38.3倍，而同期该平台季度总收入仅增长了8.9倍。 这意味着越来越多的图书正在争夺缓慢增长、有限的收入池，导致市场出现明显的“稀释效应”。

令人担忧的是，这种影响不仅限于低质量内容；即使是没有任何可检测到的人工智能文本的普通书籍也受到了影响。 在统计涵盖的八种主要图书类型中，非人工智能文本的每本书收入在七类中出现下降。 研究指出，含有大量人工智能内容的图书占目录的20%，但对销量和收入的贡献分别仅为12.1%和11.3%。 相反，没有可检测到的人工智能文本的书籍仍然占主流收入的 72.5%。 然而，随着AI书籍不断攀升畅销书排行榜榜首，新一期Top 25榜单中AI作品的比例已高达31%。

此外，分析发现，一些多产的作者使用人工智能显着提高了他们的产出，一些作者仅通过几本书就赚取了数百万美元。 从语言特征来看，畅销的人工智能书籍与现有已出版作品的重合度很高，比典型的文学作品更多地依赖生僻表达。

行业专家认为，这项研究为正在进行的人工智能版权诉讼提供了关键的实证数据。 过去，人工智能公司经常以人类阅读和学习为由来为自己辩护。 然而，市场稀释和语言重叠的证据可能会对未来有关合理使用的司法判决产生深远影响。
